messages.subject: Error in inla.inlaprogram.has.crashed()
parts:
Hi, this is Mike Crossley, a postdoc at University of Georgia, USA, new to INLA but not R.

I'm sorry to be asking probably the most vague and common question, but I'm not sure how to get past this error. Looking through previous questions/comments related to mine, I can't make out that I have a column naming issue or limitation due to computer memory. I am including my input data, code, and error message, and wonder if someone could give advice on how to proceed?

A subset of my data is attached, as well as the input graph.

I ran the following:

##################################################################################

# Import data
sample_data= read.table('sample_data.txt',sep=' ',as.is=T,check.names=F,header=T)
g1 <- inla.read.graph('./nb1.graph')

# Make model
form1 <- ln.N.butterflies ~ -1 +
  # cell ICAR random intercepts
  f(alpha_i, model="besag", graph=g1, constr=FALSE, scale.model=TRUE,
    hyper = list(prec = list(prior = "pc.prec", param = c(1, 0.01)))) +
  # cell ICAR random effort slopes
  f(eps_i, ln.Person.hours, model="besag", graph=g1, constr=FALSE, scale.model=TRUE,
    hyper = list(prec = list(prior = "pc.prec", param = c(1, 0.01)))) +
  # cell ICAR random year slopes
  f(tau_i, std_Year, model="besag", graph=g1, constr=FALSE, scale.model=TRUE,
    hyper = list(prec = list(prior = "pc.prec", param = c(1, 0.01)))) +
  # random circle intercepts
  f(kappa_k, model="iid", constr=TRUE,
    hyper = list(prec = list(prior = "pc.prec", param = c(1, 0.01))))

# Run model
out1<- inla(form1, family="nbinomial", data=sample_data, control.compute=list(cpo=T, config=T), control.inla=list(strategy="adaptive", int.strategy="auto"), num.threads=1, debug=TRUE)

##################################################################################

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Error in inla.inlaprogram.has.crashed()
parts:
I got


*** ERROR *** INLA.Data1: NBINOMIAL likelihood is defined on
integers, but y[7] = 3.17805383035


you're using a negative binomial distribution with non-integer
observations. this is what cause the error.

please update to the most recent testing version

inla.update(testing=TRUE)

restart R/Rstudio

check

inla.doc("xpoisson")

and consider to replace nbinomial with xpoisson.

you may add a iid model to each observation to mimic the nbinomial if
you need overdispersion.

let me know if there are still problems.

H
